Web Site Of The Prohibitionist Propaganda Organization, National Families In Action,
Carries Version Of Foreign Affairs Anti-Dutch Article That They Got From Mapinc. Org 
--  How Do I Know?

May 21, 1999

The Drug Czar isn't the only one using the Foreign Affairs article forprohibitionist propaganda.
See
Drug Czar Uses Foreign Affairs Magazine Article For Anti-Dutch Propaganda,
Elevating The Lying To Official Status. Analysis By Richard Cowan

I was checking up on the web site of the prohibitionist propaganda organization, National Families in Action, http://www.emory.edu/NFIA/, and I saw that -- predictably -- they were touting the Foreign Affairs anti-Dutch embarrassment, "Half-Baked" with the following:

"Foreign Affairs: Dutch Drug Policy is Disastrous

The Drug Reform movement holds up the vaunted Dutch model of drug policy as one the United States should adopt. This analysis suggests otherwise."


At that point, for some reason, I remembered an OCR error, a computer-typo, in the original version of the story that www.Mapinc.org distributed. So I immediately clicked on the link and scrolled down, and guess what?

The Drug Czar isn't the only one using the Foreign Affairs article forprohibitionist propaganda.
See
Drug Czar Uses Foreign Affairs Magazine Article For Anti-Dutch Propaganda,
Elevating The Lying To Official Status. Analysis By Richard Cowan

I was checking up on the web site of the prohibitionist propaganda organization, National Families in Action, http://www.emory.edu/NFIA/, and I saw that -- predictably -- they were touting the Foreign Affairs anti-Dutch embarrassment, "Half-Baked" with the following:

"Foreign Affairs: Dutch Drug Policy is Disastrous

The Drug Reform movement holds up the vaunted Dutch model of drug policy as one the United States should adopt. This analysis suggests otherwise."

NFIA got their version of the FA article from Mapinc.org!

The clue? In the original Mapinc version and on the NFIA site there is the following: "Then he sells them to his dealer, whom I'll call Pieter, for between 4,000 and 5,000 guilders a kilo. Hendrik reckons that his 40-square-meter "garden" yields 35 kilos of grass a year, earning him about 20,000 guilders (about $60,000) after his expenses-not bad for a part--time activity."

The guilder is around 50 cents, so this error had jumped out at me. It should have said "about 120,000 guilders." I used the correct number when I did my analysis of the article after checking to see what the hard copy of FA said. They had the right number. They may not know anything about cannabis, but they do know currency exchange rates.

NFIA doesn’t know much about either.

Well, Mapinc is there to educate people, but I doubt if "education" is NFIA’s real interest in Mapinc. After all, Mapinc has a link to NFIA, but the prohibitionists almost never link to the anti-prohibitionists. They rightly fear the truth. Ironically, NFIA's site is provided by Emory University, because it is supposedly educational.

I would urge readers to bring this and other errors to the attention of NFIA, at nfia@mindspring.com.

Just tell them that there is a typo that they missed when they cribbed the copy from Mapinc and they can find it by comparing their version with http://www.marijuananews.com/foreign_affairs_pushes_the_party.htm

Maybe they will learn something else. Not likely, but…
